issues.description: Method name inconsistency: the problem statement (method printFarmSong()) instructs students to implement a method named printFarmSong() in Farm.java, but both the template and the provided solution define and use a method named singFarmSong(). This mismatch between the documented API (printFarmSong) and the actual code (singFarmSong) can confuse students about which method to implement and which name tests or example code expect.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either update the problem statement and UML to refer to singFarmSong(), or add a public printFarmSong() method in Farm that delegates to the existing singFarmSong() (and update any example code and tests to use the same name). Ensure all references in the description, UML, template, solution, and tests use the same method identifier.

issues.description: The exercise concept is the Farm method that plays/prints the Old MacDonald song. The problem statement (UML and Part 3 task text) refers to a method named printFarmSong(), while both the provided template and the reference solution define the public method as singFarmSong() (and use singFarmSongVerse as the helper). This naming mismatch (problem statement: printFarmSong() vs code: singFarmSong()) prevents a clear 1:1 mapping: a student following the written tasks may look for printFarmSong() in the starter code and solution and not find it, causing confusion about which method to implement or call.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Option A (recommended, minimal): Update the problem statement (UML and task text) to refer to singFarmSong() instead of printFarmSong(), so the written requirements match the template and solution. Option B: Rename the public method in template and solution from singFarmSong() to printFarmSong() (and rename singFarmSongVerse to printFarmSongVerse as needed), and update the UML and task text accordingly. Ensure the chosen identifier is used consistently in UML, tasks, template code, and solution.
